title: Coolibah: Ancient Coolibah Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The eucalyptus of Australia's dry riverbeds. One was blazed DIG at Cooper Creek in 1861, and a Las Vegas park holds Nevada's largest.
intro: Coolibah is the eucalyptus of inland Australia, the shade over dry riverbeds and flood plains far from anywhere. The most famous one is the Dig Tree on Cooper Creek in Queensland, where on 21 April 1861 William Brahe blazed the word DIG over a cache of buried supplies as he abandoned the depot camp; Burke and Wills died near the creek within months. Queensland gazetted a small reserve around it in 1964. Near Lightning Ridge in New South Wales, a reader sent us a coolibah they put at about 500 years old, with a trunk of 7.5 metres, which are their figures and not a measurement we have seen. The odd one out is in Las Vegas. The Nevada Big Tree Register measured the coolibah in Winchester Park in 2015 at 70 feet tall, the largest recorded in the state.
